name: cloudflare-d1-sqlite
about: Cloudflare D1 (SQLite) at marginal paid prices, allowance 0 (C10). D1 runs SQLite and bills rows read and rows written like a Durable Object, so the candidate's own row meters are priced with no store shape. Every price is read by meter name from the dated price sheets (root price_sheets: cloudflare-d1-paid.json and cloudflare-r2-standard.json, as of 2026-10-28, official pages). One database per seat; a D1 database holds at most 10 GB, so a seat past that (the heavy profile's 26.5 GB of starting data) needs its records split over several databases, which this model does not charge for because D1 bills no per-database fee.

prices.basis: D1 bills rows scanned. SQLite loop visits are the local proxy, as for the Durable Object model (CAL-5).
Price sheet: each write to an indexed column adds one extra row written. Counted per changed index key.
Sealed history generations are R2 PUTs (Class A), beside D1 in the same Cloudflare account.
Cold-tier point reads are R2 GETs (Class B).

latency.basis: AI assumption copied from the Durable Object model (in-colo Worker to SQLite call); used only when a run simulates queueing at this placement, never by the usage table, which prices saved meters.

unpriced.item: Workers requests and CPU in front of D1
unpriced.why: D1 bills no per-query request; the Worker that queries it is priced in cloudflare-workers-paid.json ($0.30 per million requests) and the storage simulation does not model the Worker hop
D1 has no alarms; the simulated runs wake per-store alarms, which on D1 would be Cron Triggers or Queues, priced in their own sheets and not modelled; the rows each wake reads and writes are priced

unpriced.item: Workers Paid $5 per month and the included allowances
unpriced.why: one per Cloudflare account, shared by every customer of the hosted service, so not a per-team charge
archive_bytes is reported but only one storage gauge is priced
counted as attempted; whether billed is unknown (CAL-7)
